summary: The documents collectively describe the implementation of Google ReCaptcha in an ASP.NET web application. It involves server-side verification of the ReCaptcha response, localization handling, and integration with the HSPnet system.
purpose: To secure an ASP.NET application using Google ReCaptcha by verifying human interaction on forms.

workflows.name: ReCaptcha Verification Workflow
steps: User interacts with ReCaptcha widget on the web form.
ReCaptcha widget generates a token upon successful completion.
Token is sent to the server via a hidden form field upon form submission.
Server verifies the token with Google's ReCaptcha API.
If verification succeeds, user session is validated and redirected to the HSPnet start screen.
If user session is invalid, redirect to TimedOut page.
If token verification fails, user is redirected back to the ReCaptcha page.

business_rules: If the user session is not valid, redirect to a TimedOut page.
Use different headers depending on the user's locale.
validations: Perform client-side and server-side verification of the ReCaptcha token.
Ensure the ReCaptcha token is valid and not expired.
conditions: User session validity is checked before redirecting to the start screen.
Locale is determined either from the URL query string or from the user session.
system_behavior: The system supports localization by switching headers based on the user's locale.
Clears session info once the information is consumed.
Handles ReCaptcha token expiration and errors using callbacks.
exceptions: Invalid or expired ReCaptcha token results in redirecting back to the ReCaptcha page.
Absence of valid locale defaults to the default locale settings.
